scope: Owned profiles with exact Glasgow surname at birth and an indexed birth or death year through 1600 inclusive; father links only.
method: Reviewed all 21 uncertain father links and all 10 fatherless subjects against the existing cited biographies, maintained case evidence and candidate inventory. John’s sibling manuscript passage and published burgess entry were re-inspected. No new archival discovery is claimed.

results.name: David Glasgow
results.assessment: Andrew Glasgow-3163 remains a possible father; no positive relationship or identity bridge has been found. The corrected testament does not name David as a son. This removes the claimed direct proof but omission from dispositive clauses does not exclude him as a child. No positive bridge establishes his father.
results.source_summary: FamilySearch X1BJ-22S (Elspeth, 2 Mar 1606) and X1BJ-LR9 (Issobell, 3 May 1612) name David as father. Andrew's original testament, NRS CC8/8/32 images 123-124 (6 Feb 1597/8), names son Robert and daughters Marion, Jonet and Isobel, but no David.
results.next_question: Search Calder/Linlithgow land, rental or testament records for a patronymic.
results.evidence_provenance: Maintained case evidence and source locators; no new original inspection claimed for this subject.

results.name: John Glasgow
results.assessment: Ninian's 1596 burgess admission expressly names Robert Glasgow, fisher, as his father; Ninian's 1613 testament expressly calls John his brother. Shared surname, compatible chronology and Ninian's son Robert's appearance at the 1619 baptism support a common father. Confident combined-evidence inference for the record-defined brother represented by Glasgow-1030; identification with the 1618 Jonet Mathie husband remains probable.
results.next_question: Find an occupation/property bridge to the 1618 husband; father confidence applies to the record-defined brother.
results.evidence_provenance: Existing cited biography and maintained findings; sibling passage and burgess transcription re-inspected for Glasgow-1030 only.

results.name: Robert Glasgow
results.assessment: William remains the leading probable father on the combined property/craft evidence. results.next_question: Find an explicit succession or family settlement connecting Robert to William; the fisher network already supports a probable relationship.
results.evidence_provenance: Existing cited biography and maintained findings; sibling passage and burgess transcription re-inspected for Glasgow-1030 only.

results.name: Alan Glasgow
results.assessment: John Glasgw of Stirling (Space:John_Glasgw_of_Stirling), active 1475-1480; possible father/brother/uncle-generation comparison, no exact relationship. Stirling and Jedburgh have no shared associate/property/kin bridge; the record cannot distinguish father from brother, nephew or unrelated namesake.
results.source_summary: Pitcairn, Criminal Trials, vol. I pt. I, p. 19, prints the Jedburgh justice-ayre remission for the 'Slaughter of Alan Glasgw'; underlying NRS JC1/1. It names Pilmure and surety Ralph Ker, no kin. The correct date is 1495, not the misprinted 1594-5.
results.next_question: Search the Jedburgh and Stirling records for a kinship, property or associate bridge.

results.name: Barbara Glasgow
results.assessment: Ninian Glasgow (Glasgow-3188), possible father or uncle. The two dates may be proclamation and marriage. Barbara may also be the Little mother Glasgow-567 or Johnstoun wife Glasgow-3302; no continuity or father wording exists.
results.source_summary: South Leith OPR 692/2 90/219 gives Barbara Glasgow and Johne Wilsoune, 20 Sep 1611; FamilySearch XYML-ZBB gives 26 Nov 1611. Ninian's 1613 testament (CC9/7/9 images 142-145) proves son Robert and names no Barbara. Robert was a cordiner; Ninian's possible son William was in Leith, making the craft/locality pattern a useful lead.
